text:
Maya: quick sync — ran the collector holdback sampling run on ember-13b quantized (4-bit GPTQ) and wanted to share initial observations
Samir: nice, what's the experiment setup?
Maya: holdback design: 10% of requests are sampled and served with sampler=v2 (speculative branch) while 90% baseline uses greedy prefill+single-sample path. captured tokens, latencies, and top-k distributions.
Ignacio: how big was the evaluation set?
Maya: 2.5k prompts (mix: 40% user chat, 40% longform, 20% instruction). kept same temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95.
Ashley: any immediate quality regressions?
Maya: small but measurable: sampler branch shows +0.7% perplexity and a 1.2 point drop on our micro-ROUGE-L on longform subset. conversely, latency median improved from 120ms -> 88ms (token generation) on staging infra.
Cheng: was the quantization different between branches?
Maya: both used the same GPTQ 4-bit artifact. we also ran a quick int8 run locally — quality slightly better than 4-bit (ROUGE back to baseline) but 10–15% slower.
Samir: is the ROUGE drop concentrated on any prompt types?
Maya: yes — instruct prompts that need factual recall and multi-sentence coherence. single-turn chat w/short responses unaffected.
Ignacio: can you paste the sample diffs where the model diverged?
Maya: sure — excerpt:```
PROMPT: Summarize the implications of the new tax ruling for small businesses.
BASELINE: The new ruling changes deduction timelines and increases reporting requirements. Small businesses should review payroll schedules and consult tax counsel for compliance.
SAMPLER:v2: New rules shift deduction timing; businesses may need to adjust accounting practices. Also consider consulting an advisor on reporting deadlines and exemptions.
NOTES: sampler tends to compress causal chains, dropping the payroll-specific action in a few runs.
```
Ashley: hmm that's subtle but could affect downstream customer-facing summaries.
Samir: do you have confidence intervals? could be noise at 2.5k sample size.
Maya: 95% bootstrap CI for ROUGE delta on longform: [-1.9, -0.5] (so likely real).
Cheng: what's the hypothesis — sampler introduces token bias during speculative decoding that hurts multi-step coherence?
Ignacio: possibility: early token prefetch + rescore heuristics occasionally prune tokens that later become critical for long-tail factual continuity.
Maya: agrees. we instrumented KV-hit rates and saw the sampler had ~12% fewer KV cache warmups for mid-length contexts (200-600 tokens) — suggests missed prefix context.
Samir: actionable next steps?
Maya: propose a 3-step plan: 1) run targeted holdout on 10k prompts focusing on factual recall/instruction; 2) enable conservative rescoring threshold in sampler (raise accept_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.75) and re-run 5k; 3) test hybrid: sampler for short prompts only, baseline otherwise.
Ashley: for (1) we should also run the int8 artifact to see if quant interacts with sampler.
Cheng: +1. also run a cheap human eval on top 200 disagreement cases — automated metrics may miss quality nuance.
Ignacio: do we need rollout guardrails? any risk to production?
Maya: current staging run used rollout=10% and we saw no customer-facing errors. but I want an auto-fallback: if cohort ROUGE drops > 1.0 or latency > 2x, flip to baseline.
Samir: can you share the config snippet you used to spin the sampler?
Maya: paste:```
{
  "sampler": "v2",
  "speculative": true,
  "accept_threshold": 0.6,
  "max_prefetch_tokens": 32,
  "kv_warmup": "auto"
}
```
Maya: also note we observed a small regression in deterministic rerank MRR for the instruct set (~0.9% drop).
Ashley: did you correlate regression with prompt length?
Maya: yes — majority on 300-800 token range. short prompts (<80 tokens) were fine.
Cheng: for the IO side, the latency wins are real though — median token latency down ~27%, p50->p50.
Ignacio: might be worthwhile to tune the max_prefetch_tokens down for long contexts to avoid stale prefix prefetch.
Maya: tried max_prefetch_tokens=16 in a small run: coherence improved slightly, latency regressed a bit (p50 95ms).
Samir: tradeoff. maybe conditional prefetch: if prompt_len>200 then prefetch=16 else 32.
Maya: implemented conditional policy in local branch; need to run on staging.
deploy-bot: deployed collector-sampler:v2 -> staging (tag: collector-sampler/2026-03-21T15:04Z) :robot_face:
Ashley: nice. timeline for next 10k run?
Maya: starting tomorrow morning on staging with int8 + 4-bit arms, expecting 24h to finish. will post summary and diff set.
Samir: please include per-prompt signal: prefix-kv-hit, rerank-accept, top1-prob-drop, and token-level entropy.
Maya: noted. adding to the runlist.
Ignacio: if the int8 arm recovers ROUGE but increases latency a bit, we should quantify the cost delta. Redwood Optimize should be able to suggest quant+batch configs.
Cheng: yes — also include per-token cost estimate (from cost model) so we can compute unit economics for each config.
Maya: sound plan. final ask — if anyone has existing holdout prompt sets heavy on multi-step factual tasks, drop them in /mnt/holdouts/sampler_longform_2026.
Ashley: uploaded 600 prompts to that path.
Samir: thanks, team. looking forward to the 24h run. :thumbsup:
